key_insight: The paper shows that multi-agent LLM aggregation can be improved by controlling stylistic bias during answer selection and deliberately injecting bias to reveal when agents are unreliable.
engineering_relevance: It provides a test-time aggregation strategy that needs no validation set or prior model-ranking, making it practical for heterogeneous LLM systems in mathematical reasoning workflows.
method: Normalize each distinct answer into one reasoning trace to reduce majority and style bias.
Force each aggregator’s preferred answer into the minority to induce decision instability as a reliability signal.
Use this signal to choose final answers and improve aggregation without changing debate or synthesis pipelines.
evidence_signal: The method reports higher average accuracy and better token efficiency than non-oracle aggregation baselines across three math benchmarks and four heterogeneous LLM pairings, and it also improves multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents final accuracy.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on induced instability and style normalization, its gains may be sensitive to prompt design, answer formatting, and the specific mix of models involved.
paper_title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
